items.title: Wrongly recognized platform, unnecessary rebuilds
items.reason: Exact FreeBSD analogue: locally built wheel metadata used a lowercase BSD release/amd64 tag while uv generated an uppercase release and incompatible architecture spelling.

items.title: Improve BSD tag construction
items.reason: Fixed astral-sh/uv#15799 by lowercasing the FreeBSD release and using BSD architecture names, but left NetBSD release casing unchanged; this is the closest historical implementation evidence.

related.search_scope: Literal searches covered NetBSD identifiers, tag fragments, and the reported incompatibility error. Conceptual searches covered BSD tag normalization, case sensitivity, platform mismatch, and local-wheel compatibility; fix-oriented searches covered closed issues, merged pull requests, and implementation history. No other NetBSD tracker or fix was found. astral-sh/uv#3824 and astral-sh/uv#13713 were inspected and ruled out because they concern libc/interpreter OS detection rather than wheel-tag comparison.

type_reason: Source confirms incorrect behavior: FreeBSD release strings are lowercased during compatible-tag construction, while NetBSD release strings are not. This produces the reported case mismatch and rejects an otherwise matching wheel. The historical FreeBSD fix never covered NetBSD, so this is a new bug rather than a duplicate or regression.
summary: astral-sh/uv#15799 and astral-sh/uv#15829 establish the equivalent FreeBSD defect and fix. The fix did not normalize NetBSD release casing, and no existing NetBSD issue or pull request tracks this case.
draft_response: Thanks, this is a bug. NetBSD compatibility-tag construction currently replaces dots and hyphens in the release but, unlike the FreeBSD path fixed in astral-sh/uv#15829, does not lowercase it. That produces `netbsd_11_0_STABLE_amd64` and prevents it from matching the wheel’s `netbsd_11_0_stable_amd64` tag. The next step is to apply the same release normalization to NetBSD and add regression coverage for this tag.
